title: optimize multi-gpu tensor-parallel NCCL scheduling, overlap comm/compute, KV cache and continuous batching
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads show reduced throughput and higher latency tail when NCCL collectives and GPU kernel scheduling do not effectively overlap communication and compute. This PR improves NCCL stream prioritization, refines kernel/stream synchronization points, and adds targeted KV-cache-friendly batching changes to increase compute/comm overlap for continuous batching workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a prioritized set of CUDA streams for TP collectives (nccl_comm_high, nccl_comm_low, compute) and an allocator for stream affinity across modules. 2) Reduce unnecessary cudaStreamSynchronize calls by deferring kernel synchronization until NVTX-scoped barriers and by making kernel completion checks non-blocking where safe. 3) Adjust NCCL launch options and groupings to use asynchronous collectives with separate comm streams and tuned CUDA graph capture points for repeated patterns. 4) Add KV cache prefetch barrier windows to allow continuous batching to start compute while remaining comms are in-flight, and add a small per-shard pending-keys queue to avoid bursts that starve comm streams. 5) Add scheduler heuristics to prefer running short compute kernels on a dedicated low-latency compute stream to reduce stragglers. 6) Tests and perf harness updates, unit tests for scheduler heuristics, and new integration microbenchmarks. Checklist: - [x] Design review with infra and runtime teams - [x] Microbenchmarking across 4xA100, 8xA100, 8xH100 clusters - [x] Added unit and integration tests - [x] Updated observability metrics for stream utilization - [x] Documentation blurb in runtime tuning guide Implementation notes: changes are in runtime/cc/ and runtime/python bindings. Kernel sync points were minimized by moving blocking waits to the end of request handling where safe. KV cache continuous-batching changes are conservative and gated behind an opt-in config (runtime.tp.enable_kv_prefetch_overlap). Related work: builds on prior NCCL tuning PRs (see pr-71234, pr-73456) and the perf-canary improvements for batching. Testing: CI ran full unit and integration suites. A flaky GPU allocator test failed on first run (gpu_alloc_test) and was rerun; final CI passed. Microbenchmarks show median throughput improvements of 18% on 4xA100 and 24% on 8xH100 for long-sequence chat workloads with batch size 16 continuous-batching enabled. 95th percentile latency reduced by ~12% in tests with KV cache warm. Rollout plan: feature gated, toggle default on in canary pool then incrementally roll out to Dedicated clusters. Observability: added metrics runtime.stream_utilization, runtime.kv_prefetch_inflight, and runtime.nccl_comm_latency.

release_notes: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel performance: NCCL stream prioritization, reduced kernel syncs, KV-cache prefetch overlap for continuous batching. Feature gated and rolled out to canary pools; opt-in flag available for private deployments.
testing_instructions: Enable runtime.tp.enable_kv_prefetch_overlap=true in runtime config, run bench/perf/microbench/tp_kvcache_overlap_bench.py against 4x/8x cluster, monitor runtime.stream_utilization and runtime.nccl_comm_latency metrics.
rollout_plan: Canary (10% capacity) -> Dedicated small pool -> full Dedicated. Monitor metrics: stream_utilization, kv_prefetch_backpressure, and request error rates. Roll back by disabling runtime.tp.enable_kv_prefetch_overlap or setting runtime.tp.disable_stream_priority=true.
notes: No API changes. Behavior is runtime-config gated for safety. Related PRs: pr-71234, pr-73456.
